inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Medication No Longer Used: There were three expired medications observed during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Medication No Longer Used (26 TAC §746.3809)

occurrences.finding: Food Allergy Emergency Plan Signed by Parents and Health Care Professional: A child had food allergy plan with appropriate signatures however, did not have the medication as required per the food allergy plan. Without this medication, the plan could not be implemented.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Food Allergy Emergency Plan Signed by Parents and Health Care Professional (26 TAC §746.3819)

occurrences.finding: Administering Medication - Original Container with Child's Name, Date: Medication listed on a child's food allergy emergency plan was not in its original box labeled with the child's name.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Administering Medication - Original Container with Child's Name, Date (26 TAC §746.3805(b)(1))

occurrences.finding: Garbage Inaccessible to Children; Maintained in Sanitary Manner: A  trashcan containing a soiled diaper, without a lid, and accessible to children was observed during the inspection.  This was corrected at inspection when a lid was added to the trashcan.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Garbage Inaccessible to Children; Maintained in Sanitary Manner (26 TAC §746.3407(8))

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: A cleaning supply spray can was observed on the back of the toilet in a bathroom used by children. The cleaning supply spray can was accessible to children.      This was corrected at inspection when the caregiver moved the cleaning supply spray can.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk: There was sufficient evidence found during the investigation to show that the operation did not immediately notify the parent of a child when a volatile parent yelled and cursed at their child while the child was in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Parental Communication - Situation that Placed a Child at Risk (26 TAC §746.307(b)(4))

occurrences.finding: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Use of Safety Straps: It was found during an investigation that a caregiver failed to properly fasten the safety straps on a highchair as the safety straps were fastened, but not tightened, resulting in an infant climbing out of the highchair and falling to the floor, hitting their head.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Use of Safety Straps (26 TAC §746.2407)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Intervene to ensure each child's safety: There was sufficient evidence found during an investigation to support that an infant was able to climb out of a highchair and hit their head on the floor without a caregiver intervening.  One caregiver was changing a diaper, and another caregiver was sitting on the floor feeding another infant.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Intervene to ensure each child's safety (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(5))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: A caregiver did not use good judgement when they did not communicate with a parent if a child needed transportation and left the child behind at the elementary school.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times: Screen time was observed in a classroom during rest time.     This was corrected at inspection when the caregiver turned the screen off.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times (26 TAC §746.2207(c)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children's names and ages: One caregiver gave the wrong number of children in care when asked twice. This was corrected at inspection when the caregiver counted the number of children and gave the correct number.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children's names and ages (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Provide care consistent with child's habits, interests, strengths, special needs, including any special supervision needs: Information obtained throughout the investigation shows that a caregiver failed to provide care consistent with a child's special dietary needs when they did not give the child the food and drink needed for their special diet.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information-Completed Food Allergy Plan: One child did not have all of the medication listed on their food allergy plan.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information-Completed Food Allergy Plan (26 TAC §746.605(16))

occurrences.finding: CPR Training and Recertification Adhere to Guidelines-skill based: One caregiver did not have CPR training that includes hands-on skill-based instruction.
occurrences.violation_type_title: CPR Training and Recertification Adhere to Guidelines-skill based (26 TAC §746.1315(b)(1))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: Information obtained throughout the investigation shows that a child sustained an injury when a caregiver left a backpack with scissors in it accessible to children, resulting in a child cutting another child's finger with the scissors.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: There was a caregiver present who was caring for children and who did not have a cleared background check.     The caregiver left during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: During a DFPS investigation, it was found that a caregiver grabbed and pulled a child in care inappropriately.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children responsible for: Two caregivers did not know how old the children were that they were responsible for.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pediatric First Aid with Rescue Breathing: There was a caregiver who had unsupervised access to children in care without current certification in first aid.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Training Requirements for Employees, Caregivers, and Directors - Pediatric First Aid with Rescue Breathing (26 TAC §746.1301(a)(3)(A))

occurrences.finding: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited: During an investigation there was sufficient evidence to support a child was abused.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Hitting with Hand or Instrument: In the act of redirecting a child's behavior a caregiver hit a child with an open hand on their face.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Hitting with Hand or Instrument (26 TAC §746.2805(4))

occurrences.finding: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited: During an investigation there was sufficient evidence to support a child was abused.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))

occurrences.finding: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation: During an investigation inspection caregivers interviewed admitted to the use of time outs. These time outs were explained as placing a child behind the diaper changing station so they cannot see the other children having fun and lasting five minutes or more.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation (26 TAC §746.2803(4)(D))
